chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Aban from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Qunut and what is said in it, so he said: 'Whatever God has decreed upon your tongue, and I do not know anything specific/limited in it.'
ai.seo_question: What should be recited during Qunut in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the nature of Qunut by stating that any supplication flowing naturally from the heart is acceptable, as he knew of no fixed, limited text prescribed for it. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of Qunut as a flexible, voluntary supplication rather than a rigidly codified obligation, allowing for personal expression of devotion during prayer. The emphasis on 'what is on your tongue' highlights the importance of sincerity and ease in worship, distinguishing it from the mandatory recitations of the Quran.
